newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week to July 4.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse turnover up in week to July 4.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) reported on Friday a 68.6 percent increase in its turnover in the first four days of the week ending July 4.
Total turnover rose to 150.712 million dinars in 135 transactions from 82.107 million in 139 deals a week ago, the bourse said.
The BSE was closed on July 4 because of the public holiday. It will remain closed on Monday, July 7, for another public holiday.
For the week ending July 4, the BSE reported the following details:
* Commercial paper accounted for 120 transactions worth 19.012 million dinars.
* Treasury bills traded three times for a volume of 0.46 million dinars.
Interest rates on commercial paper and treasury bills ranged between 6.0 and 13 percent per month, while maturity stood between seven and 90 days.
* There were six transactions in the central bank short-term bonds worth 129.500 million dinars.
* On the secondary market, the BSE reported two deals worth 0.540 million dinars, with the National Bank of Yugoslavia selling bonds from its portfolio issued by the Serbian Commodity Reserve Agency.
* There were two transactions of wheat forward contracts worth 0.17 million dinars.
* Two deals were in certificates of deposits in the volume of 1.03 million dinars.
* Over-the-counter trade in commercial paper and treasury bills fell slightly to 40.587 million dinars from 41.097 million the previous week.
* OTC trade in giro money, with banks trading their surplus liquidity, declined to 17.45 million from 23.645 million. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 311 4254 ($1=5.7809 Yugoslav dinars)
